title.en: Good microbes: curd, idli and digestion

text.en: Disha watches her mother make idlis. The batter rises and becomes fluffy. What makes it rise?

Not all microbes are bad. Some are helpful.
Microbes in the air help make idli batter rise. They are the reason the batter becomes light and fluffy overnight.
Curd is made with microbes too. Small microbes in curd join the good microbes in the stomach to help in digestion.
Aditya Anna has an upset stomach after eating food at a fair. Curd or buttermilk may be given as a home remedy. If the problem is severe, we must consult a doctor.
Sometimes bad eating habits can also lead to indigestion.
Many traditional practices related to food are passed on in families from one generation to another. Disha's case diary 'My Food, My Pride' records them.
Seasonal fruits are fresh and tasty. Lychees come in the rainy season and local mangoes in summer; waiting for the season makes eating them a joy.
(additional, not in the textbook) After food is eaten it is broken down in the stomach and intestines so that the body can take what it needs.

problem.en: Name two foods that need good microbes to be made.

text.en: Curd is made with microbes in milk.
Idli batter rises with microbes.
So curd and idli use good microbes.

prompt.en: Why are some microbes called good microbes?

requiredIdeas.en: They help make curd and idli

points.en: Curd and idli batter need microbes.
